# cothon

> A dashboard for a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner: every job it runs, across repos, in a web UI, with the queue, CPU and memory per job, rerun/cancel, and runner control.

It reads the runner's own diagnostic logs (`~/actions-runner/_diag`), so it needs no GitHub admin rights and shows a job the moment it starts. Named after the cothon, Carthage's circular war harbour watched from the admiral's tower at its centre.

## Features

- Every job the runner executes, grouped by repo and workflow run, or as a flat list; filters live in the URL
- The running job with live CPU, memory and process count; finished jobs keep average CPU and peak memory
- Jobs queued for this runner (asked from GitHub for the repos it worked on recently)
- Rerun a job, rerun failed jobs, cancel a run (through the GitHub CLI)
- Runner control: start detached, stop or restart after the current job, follow its logs, optional login service (systemd on Linux, launchd on macOS) that restarts it on crash
- Desktop notifications when jobs finish (notify-send on Linux, Notification Center on macOS)
- Loopback-only server with one-time sign-in links; light and dark themes

## Install

Linux and macOS. Needs Go 1.24+; the GitHub CLI (logged in) for rerun, cancel and the queue.

```
go install github.com/aymenkrifa/cothon/cmd/cothon@latest
```

## Usage

```
cothon web                  # open the web UI (server runs in the background)
cothon status               # server and runner status, CPU and memory
cothon runner start         # start the runner detached
cothon runner stop          # stop after the current job (--force: now)
cothon runner logs -f       # follow what the runner prints
cothon runner enable        # start at login, restart on crash
cothon update               # install the latest version (go install)
```
